report.summary: An order placement incident occurred starting at 13:31 UTC on 2026-10-10, impacting orders-service and mobile-bff with 'Please try again' errors and failed order placements. The root cause is identified as a high-volume push notification campaign ('diwali_sip_offer') sent by notification-service to 2.1 million users at 13:30 with a deep link to 'orders/new-sip'. This campaign triggered a massive, synchronized traffic influx starting at 13:31, overwhelming orders-service's internal executor queue (capacity 500) and causing RejectedExecutionException errors, high CPU utilization, and spiked latencies.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Diwali SIP Campaign Push Notification Traffic Surge

supporting.note: Push campaign sent to 2.1M users at 13:30, precisely preceding the 13:31 traffic surge onset.
Notification service logs confirm dispatch of the push campaign at 13:30.
Shows sudden RPS increase starting at 13:31.
Shows sudden RPS increase starting at 13:31, surging from baseline 115 req/s to 748+ req/s.
orders-service logged RejectedExecutionException due to order-executor queue full starting at 13:32.
Notification-service health metrics retrieved and verified stable during campaign window.
Notification-service memory usage verified stable during campaign window.
Notification-service error rate verified stable during campaign window.
Notification-service latency verified stable during campaign window.
orders-service previously received 429 Too Many Requests from broker-api.

contradicting.note: Broker-API 429 warnings occurred earlier at 12:31, whereas the incident onset and massive RPS surge strictly correlate with the 13:30 push campaign.

facts.text: notification-service launched the 'diwali_sip_offer' push campaign to 2.1M users with deep link 'orders/new-sip' at 2026-10-10T13:30:00+00:00.
orders-service experienced an RPS anomaly onset starting at 2026-10-10T13:31:00+00:00, surging from a baseline of ~115 req/s to a peak of 872.67 req/s.
mobile-bff experienced an RPS anomaly starting at 2026-10-10T13:31:00+00:00.
orders-service error rate and latency anomalies began at 2026-10-10T13:32:00+00:00, with error rates peaking at 15.85% and p99 latency peaking at 8,999.2 ms.
orders-service started logging RejectedExecutionException due to order-executor queue full (capacity 500) starting at 2026-10-10T13:32:04+00:00.
mobile-bff experienced an error rate anomaly starting at 13:32:00+00:00, peaking at 4.42% error rate.
orders-service CPU usage spiked up to 106.54% and reached maximum autoscaler replicas (6/6) at 13:50:19.
notification-service health metrics (CPU, memory, error rate, p99 latency) showed no anomalies during the push campaign window.

assumptions: The push notification deep link successfully drove immediate concurrent user sessions that exceeded provisioned orders-service baseline capacity before autoscaling took full effect.

recommended_actions.action: Implement rate limiting or throttling on inbound traffic originating from bulk push notification deep links to prevent downstream thread pool saturation.
recommended_actions.rationale: Unrestricted deep link traffic from large-scale campaigns directly caused the thread pool exhaustion and subsequent order placement failures.

recommended_actions.action: Increase the default executor queue capacity and adjust the autoscaling thresholds/policies for orders-service to absorb sudden marketing campaign traffic spikes more smoothly.
recommended_actions.rationale: orders-service hit its maximum replica limit (6/6) and filled its executor queue (capacity 500), resulting in high error rates.

recommended_actions.action: Establish a coordination and staggering protocol between marketing teams dispatching large push campaigns and platform on-calls to pre-scale target services.
recommended_actions.rationale: Unannounced high-volume traffic campaigns can bypass normal provisioning windows and cause sudden system degradation.
